images.title: The value of each digit
images.purpose: Show the place value chart with the new TTh column, the times 10 step from one place to the next, and the value of each digit of 52,525.
images.composition: A chart with a digit row and a value row, four curved ×10 arrows above its headers, and the whole number written large below.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Centre: a table with 6 columns and 3 rows: a narrow left label column (about 180 px) then 5 equal columns (about 210 px each). Header row: the left cell is empty, then TTh, Th, H, T, O left to right in white bold letters on blue #0072B2 cells, except the TTh cell, which is reddish purple #CC79A7 with dark letters (the new column). Row 1: the left cell reads Digit, then the digits 5, 2, 5, 2, 5 in large bold dark numerals (90 px). Row 2: the left cell reads Value, then 50,000, 2,000, 500, 20, 5 in bold dark numerals (50 px), each centred under its digit. Above the 5 header cells, 4 curved amber #E69F00 arrows, each running from one header to the next header on its left and pointing left: O to T, T to H, H to Th, Th to TTh. Each arrow carries the label ×10 above it. Below the table, centred, the number 52,525 in very large bold dark numerals (120 px) with the comma clearly drawn, the largest text in the frame.

images.takeaway: Each place is worth 10 times the place on its right, so the three 5s in 52,525 are worth 50,000, 500 and 5.
images.description: A place value chart with columns TTh, Th, H, T, O holding the digits 5, 2, 5, 2, 5 and their values 50,000, 2,000, 500, 20, 5, with four ×10 arrows above and 52,525 below.
images.context: Concept image for The new TTh column and the value of digits. It keeps the chart and the ×10 arrows of the figure in your maths book and fills the chart with the video's own example, 52,525.
images.teaching_notes: Point out that the same digit 5 has three different values because of its place. The arrows read from right to left: ten of one place make one of the next place on the left. TTh is coloured differently because it is the new column.

image_decisions.why: The chart with ×10 arrows and a worked number shows why a digit's value depends on its place.
